questions.question: What can speed up alcohol leaving your body?

options.text: Nothing. Only time removes all alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing. Only time removes all alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes about 90 percent of alcohol from your body. It works at a constant rate of about one drink per hour for all people. It cannot work faster.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain or fog. Pay attention to vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. Driving after alcohol or drugs is unsafe. Driving after both is even more dangerous.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and never follow too closely behind them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows a lane for left turns only from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:
questions.explanation: Driving below the speed limit is dangerous. Slow drivers force other cars to follow closely or take risks to pass. You should follow the posted minimum speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The safest speed for a residential area.
The safest speed for an expressway exit.
The safest speed for an expressway entrance.
The safest speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safest speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safest speed to use when exiting a highway. In this example, it shows 30 mph.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is coming up ahead.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, near pedestrians or hazards, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that traffic only moves in one direction. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to a traffic light ahead. Be ready to stop for red lights and watch for other traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay safe by doing all of these: avoid eye contact, don't make gestures at them, and move away from them. Slow down or change lanes to put distance between you and the angry driver.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel. Make sure any passengers keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Tiredness affects your driving as much as alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you as much as a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours impairs you as much as a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means no. This sign says you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow diamond warning sign tells you that a lane is ending or the road is getting narrower. Be ready to move to another lane safely.

questions.question: At night, it is hardest to see:
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs or other vehicles.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine makes both stronger. For example, one drink with a cold remedy could affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Treat it the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When you get ready to change lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, look over your shoulder quickly to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not go around the gate.

questions.question: You need a driver license to:

options.text: Buckle a child into a safety seat.
Steer a vehicle while it is being towed or pushed.
Turn off child locks in a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer a vehicle while it is being towed or pushed.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to sit in the front seat of a running vehicle without a driver license. You also cannot steer a vehicle from the front seat while it is being pushed or towed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may cross the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle coming. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down, clear a path for it, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, ____ has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. When the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the rest of the procession can follow through, even if traffic signals say to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection carefully, without always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a full stop and let vehicles and pedestrians in or near the intersection go first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If your license is suspended a third time because of the point system, how long will it be suspended?
questions.explanation: In North Carolina, your license can be suspended if you collect too many points from traffic violations. A first suspension lasts 60 days. A third suspension lasts 12 months.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles that are already in the roundabout.
